claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by a dynamically regenerated hybrid protective layer combining a wear-induced tribofilm with a passive oxide film.
The hybrid protective layer reduces material removal caused by wear.
The hybrid protective layer reduces chemical attack caused by corrosion.
The diversity of alloying elements enables formation of the hybrid protective layer.
The proposed initial alloy is multiphase and has a homogeneous distribution of multiple principal elements.
The proposed initial alloy possesses a thin, incompletely developed passive oxide film.
A combined sliding-wear and chloride-corrosion test can be compared with separate wear-only and corrosion-only tests under matched conditions.
During combined exposure, a wear-induced tribofilm integrates with an element-derived passive oxide layer.
The alloy's diverse elements facilitate rapid regeneration of the passive oxide layer during chemical attack.
The alloy's diverse elements stabilize the regenerated passive oxide layer.
Mechanical wear partially removes the passive oxide layer.
Mechanical action generates a tribofilm from oxidized and mechanically mixed phases.
The generated tribofilm rapidly reestablishes a barrier against further abrasion and corrosion.
Combined wear-corrosion material loss will be lower than the sum of losses measured in wear-only and corrosion-only tests.
Hybrid-film regeneration will produce lower mass loss and less surface damage than in a baseline lacking an effective protective mechanism.
The protective effect holds only when simultaneous mechanical and corrosive intensities permit dynamic film regeneration.
The protective effect may fail when corrosion aggressiveness or wear rate exceeds the alloy's capacity to maintain the hybrid layer.
The protective effect may fail when the wear mechanism completely disrupts oxide formation.
Failure to observe significantly lower combined degradation than the sum of separate-test degradation would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to detect a hybrid protective film by surface analysis would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The comparator is defined inconsistently: the intervention compares combined exposure with separate tests on the same alloy, the baseline describes a different control alloy subjected separately, and the falsification design subjects both alloys to combined and separate tests.
